WebFetch truncated both DailyMed renderings before the DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION section, so all dosing statements are cited to CDC [2], not the label. 2026-11-23: the SPL XML fetch includes Dosage and Administration, so the 150 mg single-dose statement is now also cited to the label. Label inconsistency noted: Clinical Pharmacology reports oral contraceptive AUC increases of 25% (levonorgestrel) and 38% (ethinyl estradiol) at 200 mg daily, while Precautions reports 40% and 24%; the guide FAQ quotes the Precautions wording. Alcohol: a full-text search of the label for "alcohol" and "ethanol" finds only the chemical name (benzyl alcohol) and no interaction or warning; the alcohol FAQ says the label does not list alcohol among its interactions.

claims.text: Fluconazole is a triazole antifungal (Diflucan brand)
claims.quote: DIFLUCAN® (fluconazole), the first of a new subclass of synthetic triazole antifungal agents

claims.text: blocks lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, which converts lanosterol to ergosterol
claims.quote: Fluconazole is a highly selective inhibitor of fungal cytochrome P450 dependent enzyme lanosterol 14-α-demethylase. This enzyme functions to convert lanosterol to ergosterol.

claims.text: loss of normal sterols may be responsible for fungistatic effect
claims.quote: The subsequent loss of normal sterols correlates with the accumulation of 14-α-methyl sterols in fungi and may be responsible for the fungistatic activity of fluconazole.

claims.text: more than 90 percent of an oral dose is absorbed
claims.quote: the bioavailability of orally administered fluconazole is over 90% compared with intravenous administration.

claims.text: plasma half-life about 30 hours (range 20 to 50)
claims.quote: terminal plasma elimination half-life of approximately 30 hours (range: 20 to 50 hours)

claims.text: single 150 mg dose reached vaginal tissue and vaginal fluid
claims.quote: A single oral 150 mg dose of fluconazole administered to 27 patients penetrated into vaginal tissue ... A single oral 150 mg dose of fluconazole administered to 14 patients penetrated into vaginal fluid

claims.text: can be taken with or without food
claims.quote: exposure to the drug is not affected by food. Therefore, DIFLUCAN may be taken without regard to meals.

claims.text: use in pregnancy should be avoided except severe or life-threatening fungal infections, when benefit outweighs risk
claims.quote: Use in pregnancy should be avoided except in patients with severe or potentially life-threatening fungal infections in whom fluconazole may be used if the anticipated benefit outweighs the possible risk to the fetus.

claims.text: epidemiological studies suggest potential risk after 150 mg single or repeated dose in first trimester; limitations, not confirmed in controlled trials
claims.quote: Epidemiological studies suggest a potential risk of spontaneous abortion and congenital abnormalities in infants whose mothers were treated with 150 mg of fluconazole as a single or repeated dose in the first trimester, but these epidemiological studies have limitations

claims.text: findings not confirmed in controlled clinical trials
claims.quote: these findings have not been confirmed in controlled clinical trials.

claims.text: high doses 400 to 800 mg/day during most or all of first trimester: distinct pattern of birth defects
claims.quote: Case reports describe a pattern of distinct congenital anomalies in infants exposed in utero to high dose maternal fluconazole (400 to 800 mg/day) during most or all of the first trimester.

claims.text: low levels in breast milk after single 150 mg dose; caution in nursing woman
claims.quote: Fluconazole was present in low levels in breast milk following administration of a single 150 mg dose ... Caution should be exercised when DIFLUCAN is administered to a nursing woman.

claims.text: side effects 26 percent vs 16 percent intravaginal in U.S. comparative studies
claims.quote: a higher incidence of drug related adverse events with DIFLUCAN (26%) versus intravaginal agents (16%) in U.S. comparative clinical studies.

claims.text: headache 13, nausea 7, abdominal pain 6, diarrhea 3 percent
claims.quote: were headache (13%), nausea (7%), and abdominal pain (6%) ... diarrhea (3%), dyspepsia (1%), dizziness (1%), and taste perversion (1%)

claims.text: rare serious liver reactions; caution with liver dysfunction; stop if liver disease signs
claims.quote: there have been rare cases of serious hepatic reactions during treatment with DIFLUCAN ... DIFLUCAN should be administered with caution to patients with liver dysfunction. DIFLUCAN should be discontinued if clinical signs and symptoms consistent with liver disease develop

claims.text: rare anaphylaxis and angioedema; exfoliative skin disorders
claims.quote: Rarely, angioedema and anaphylactic reaction have been reported in marketing experience. ... Exfoliative skin disorders during treatment with DIFLUCAN have been reported.

claims.text: moderate CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inhibitor, strong CYP2C19 inhibitor
claims.quote: Fluconazole is a moderate CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inhibitor. Fluconazole is also a strong inhibitor of CYP2C19.

claims.text: effect persists 4 to 5 days after stopping due to long half-life
claims.quote: The enzyme inhibiting effect of fluconazole persists 4 to 5 days after discontinuation of fluconazole treatment due to the long half-life of fluconazole.

claims.text: warfarin: prothrombin time can rise; monitoring and dose adjustment
claims.quote: Prothrombin time may be increased in patients receiving concomitant DIFLUCAN and coumarin-type anticoagulants. ... Dose adjustment of warfarin may be necessary.

claims.text: statins atorvastatin, simvastatin: myopathy and rhabdomyolysis
claims.quote: The risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis increases when fluconazole is coadministered with HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors metabolized through CYP3A4, such as atorvastatin and simvastatin

claims.text: rare QT prolongation and torsade; erythromycin, pimozide, quinidine contraindicated
claims.quote: there have been rare cases of QT prolongation and torsade de pointes in patients taking fluconazole. ... such as erythromycin, pimozide, and quinidine are contraindicated

claims.text: phenytoin levels rise
claims.quote: DIFLUCAN increases the plasma concentrations of phenytoin.

claims.text: sulfonylureas glipizide, glyburide, tolbutamide levels rise; hypoglycemia
claims.quote: DIFLUCAN reduces the metabolism of tolbutamide, glyburide, and glipizide and increases the plasma concentration of these agents. ... one fatality has been reported from hypoglycemia in association with combined DIFLUCAN and glyburide use.

claims.text: oral contraceptives: EE and LNG up 40 and 24 percent at 200 mg daily; unlikely to affect efficacy
claims.quote: at 200 mg daily, the AUCs of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel were increased 40% and 24%, respectively. ... multiple-dose use of fluconazole at these doses is unlikely to have an effect on the efficacy of the combined oral contraceptive.

claims.text: Vaginal candidiasis is a labeled indication
claims.quote: Vaginal candidiasis (vaginal yeast infections due to Candida).

claims.text: Recommended dose for vaginal candidiasis is 150 mg as a single oral dose
claims.quote: The recommended dosage of DIFLUCAN for vaginal candidiasis is 150 mg as a single oral dose.

claims.text: Peak plasma levels 1 to 2 hours after a dose in fasting volunteers
claims.quote: Peak plasma concentrations (Cmax) in fasted normal volunteers occur between 1 and 2 hours

claims.text: Vaginal tissue ratios 0.94 to 1.14 over first 48 hours; vaginal fluid over first 72 hours
claims.quote: penetrated into vaginal tissue, resulting in tissue: plasma ratios ranging from 0.94 to 1.14 over the first 48 hours ... penetrated into vaginal fluid ... over the first 72 hours following dosing.

claims.text: No renal dose adjustment for single-dose vaginal therapy
claims.quote: There is no need to adjust single dose therapy for vaginal candidiasis because of impaired renal function.

claims.text: Label US trials: one-month clinical cure 69 vs 72 percent; eradication 61 vs 60; therapeutic cure 55 percent both; 448 vs 422 enrolled
Comparator was clotrimazole or miconazole intravaginally for 7 days, evaluated at one month
claims.quote: the results of the fluconazole regimen were comparable to the control regimen (clotrimazole or miconazole intravaginally for 7 days) both clinically and statistically at the one month post-treatment evaluation.

claims.text: Fewer than 4 episodes a year: 80 percent clinical cure; 4 or more: 57 percent
claims.quote: had acute vaginitis (<4 episodes/12 months) and achieved 80% clinical cure ... recurrent vaginitis (≥4 episodes/12 months) and achieved 57% clinical cure

claims.text: Side effect table: headache 13 vs 7, nausea 7 vs 1, abdominal pain 6 vs 2, diarrhea 3 vs under 1, taste 1 vs 0, application site 0 vs 5 percent
claims.quote: Headache 58 (13%) 28 (7%) ... Abdominal pain 25 (6%) 7 (2%) Nausea 30 (7%) 3 (1%) Diarrhea 12 (3%) 2 (<1%) Application site event 0 (0%) 19 (5%) Taste Perversion 6 (1%) 0 (0%)

claims.text: Most side effects mild to moderate; dyspepsia and dizziness 1 percent
claims.quote: dyspepsia (1%), dizziness (1%), and taste perversion (1%). Most of the reported side effects were mild to moderate in severity.

claims.text: Dizziness or seizures may occasionally occur; do not drive until you know how it affects you
claims.quote: When driving vehicles or operating machines, it should be taken into account that occasionally dizziness or seizures may occur. ... Do not drive or operate machinery until you know how DIFLUCAN affects you.

claims.text: Amiodarone may increase QT prolongation, caution notably with high-dose fluconazole
claims.quote: Concomitant administration of fluconazole with amiodarone may increase QT prolongation. Caution must be exercised ... notably with high-dose fluconazole (800 mg).

claims.text: Warfarin: bleeding events reported with increased prothrombin time
claims.quote: bleeding events (bruising, epistaxis, gastrointestinal bleeding, hematuria, and melena) have been reported in association with increases in prothrombin time in patients receiving fluconazole concurrently with warfarin.

claims.text: Fluvastatin also listed for myopathy risk
claims.quote: or through CYP2C9, such as fluvastatin (decreased hepatic metabolism of the statin)

claims.text: Carbamazepine levels rise; dose adjustment may be needed
claims.quote: an increase in serum carbamazepine of 30% has been observed. ... Dosage adjustment of carbamazepine may be necessary

claims.text: Calcium channel blockers: higher exposure; monitor
claims.quote: (nifedipine, isradipine, amlodipine, verapamil, and felodipine) ... Fluconazole has the potential to increase the systemic exposure of the calcium channel antagonists. Frequent monitoring for adverse events is recommended.

claims.text: Cyclosporine levels rise significantly; monitoring recommended
claims.quote: DIFLUCAN significantly increases cyclosporine levels ... Careful monitoring of cyclosporine concentrations and serum creatinine is recommended

claims.text: Fentanyl: delayed elimination; elevated levels may cause respiratory depression
claims.quote: fluconazole delayed the elimination of fentanyl significantly. Elevated fentanyl concentration may lead to respiratory depression.

claims.text: Celecoxib exposure more than doubled; half dose may be needed
claims.quote: the celecoxib Cmax and AUC increased by 68% and 134%, respectively. Half of the celecoxib dose may be necessary when combined with fluconazole.

claims.text: Abrocitinib: avoid concomitant use
claims.quote: Avoid concomitant use of abrocitinib with DIFLUCAN.

claims.text: Amitriptyline and nortriptyline effect increased; dose may need adjusting
claims.quote: Fluconazole increases the effect of amitriptyline and nortriptyline. ... Dosage of amitriptyline/nortriptyline should be adjusted, if necessary.

claims.text: Post-marketing QT and torsade mostly in seriously ill patients; hypokalemia and advanced heart failure increase risk
claims.quote: Most of these reports involved seriously ill patients with multiple confounding risk factors ... Patients with hypokalemia and advanced cardiac failure are at an increased risk

claims.text: Superinfection with non-albicans species such as C. krusei, often inherently not susceptible
claims.quote: cases of superinfection with Candida species other than C. albicans, which are often inherently not susceptible to DIFLUCAN (e.g., Candida krusei).

claims.text: Allergic reaction signs; stop and call provider or go to emergency room
claims.quote: Stop taking DIFLUCAN, call your healthcare provider or go to the nearest hospital emergency room right away if you get any signs or symptoms of an allergic reaction including: shortness of breath ... wheezing

claims.text: Liver problem signs: dark urine, jaundice, light stools, vomiting, loss of appetite; tell provider right away
claims.quote: Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have symptoms of serious liver problems including: dark colored urine ... yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice) light-colored stools tiredness vomiting loss of appetite

claims.text: Alcohol FAQ: label advises caution with liver dysfunction (label lists no alcohol interaction; see notes)
claims.quote: DIFLUCAN should be administered with caution to patients with liver dysfunction.

claims.text: single 150 mg oral dose for uncomplicated VVC
claims.quote: Fluconazole 150 mg orally in a single dose

claims.text: OTC intravaginal agents: clotrimazole, miconazole, tioconazole; prescription: butoconazole, terconazole; regimens from single application to 7 to 14 days
claims.quote: Clotrimazole 1% cream 5 g intravaginally daily for 7–14 days ... Tioconazole 6.5% ointment 5 g intravaginally in a single application ... Prescription Intravaginal Agents ... Butoconazole 2% cream ... Terconazole 0.4% cream

claims.text: azole treatment: relief and negative cultures in 80 to 90 percent who complete therapy
claims.quote: Treatment with azoles results in relief of symptoms and negative cultures in 80%–90% of patients who complete therapy.

claims.text: severe VVC: two 150 mg doses 72 hours apart or 7 to 14 days topical
claims.quote: Either 7–14 days of topical azole or 150 mg of fluconazole in two sequential oral doses (second dose 72 hours after initial dose) is recommended.

claims.text: recurrent VVC induction 100/150/200 mg every third day for 3 doses
claims.quote: (e.g., 7–14 days of topical therapy or a 100-mg, 150-mg, or 200-mg oral dose of fluconazole every third day for a total of 3 doses [days 1, 4, and 7]) is recommended

claims.text: maintenance weekly for 6 months
claims.quote: Oral fluconazole (i.e., a 100-mg, 150-mg, or 200-mg dose) weekly for 6 months is the indicated maintenance regimen.

claims.text: recurrent VVC usually three or more episodes in less than a year
claims.quote: usually defined as three or more episodes of symptomatic VVC in <1 year

claims.text: maintenance effective but rarely curative long-term
claims.quote: Suppressive maintenance therapies are effective at controlling recurrent VVC but are rarely curative long-term.

claims.text: pregnancy: only 7-day topical azoles
claims.quote: Only topical azole therapies, applied for 7 days, are recommended for use among pregnant women.

claims.text: single 150 mg dose might be associated with spontaneous abortion and congenital anomalies; should not be used
claims.quote: Epidemiologic studies indicate a single 150-mg dose of fluconazole might be associated with spontaneous abortion and congenital anomalies; therefore, it should not be used.

claims.text: C. glabrata and other non-albicans in 10 to 20 percent of recurrent VVC
claims.quote: C. glabrata and other non–albicans Candida species are observed in 10%–20% of women with recurrent VVC.

claims.text: conventional therapies less effective against non-albicans
claims.quote: Conventional antimycotic therapies are not as effective against these non–albicans yeasts as against C. albicans.

claims.text: culture or PCR for complicated VVC; susceptibility testing if culture positive despite maintenance
claims.quote: Vaginal culture or PCR should be obtained from women with complicated VVC ... susceptibility tests, if available, should be obtained among symptomatic patients who remain culture positive despite maintenance therapy.

claims.text: non-albicans: 7 to 14 days non-fluconazole azole
claims.quote: a longer duration of therapy (7–14 days) with a nonfluconazole azole regimen (oral or topical) is recommended.

claims.text: if recurrence, boric acid 600 mg vaginally once daily for 3 weeks
claims.quote: If recurrence occurs, 600 mg of boric acid in a gelatin capsule administered vaginally once daily for 3 weeks is indicated.

claims.text: persistent symptoms or recurrence within 2 months: evaluate and test; return for follow-up
claims.quote: women with persistent or recurrent symptoms after treatment should be instructed to return for follow-up visits. ... or who has a recurrence of symptoms <2 months after treatment for VVC should be evaluated clinically and tested.

claims.text: About 10 to 20 percent of women have complicated VVC
claims.quote: Approximately 10%–20% of women will have complicated VVC, requiring special diagnostic and therapeutic considerations.

claims.text: Box 4 classification: uncomplicated = sporadic, mild-moderate, likely C. albicans, nonimmunocompromised; complicated = recurrent, severe, non-albicans, diabetes or immunocompromise
claims.quote: Uncomplicated VVC Sporadic or infrequent VVC AND Mild-to-moderate VVC AND Likely to be Candida albicans AND Nonimmunocompromised women Complicated VVC Recurrent VVC OR Severe VVC OR Non-albicans candidiasis OR Women with diabetes, immunocompromising conditions

claims.text: Severe VVC defined as extensive vulvar erythema, edema, excoriation, fissures
claims.quote: Severe VVC (i.e., extensive vulvar erythema, edema, excoriation, and fissure formation)

claims.text: Compromised host may not respond to short therapy; 7 to 14 days needed
claims.quote: might not respond as well to short-term therapies. Efforts to correct modifiable conditions should be made, and more prolonged (i.e., 7–14 days) conventional treatment is necessary.

claims.text: Recurrent induction doses on days 1, 4 and 7
claims.quote: every third day for a total of 3 doses [days 1, 4, and 7]

claims.text: Recurrent VVC affects fewer than 5 percent of women
claims.quote: affects <5% of women but carries a substantial economic burden

claims.text: Symptoms (pruritus, soreness, dyspareunia, external dysuria, discharge) not specific
claims.quote: Typical symptoms of VVC include pruritus, vaginal soreness, dyspareunia, external dysuria, and abnormal vaginal discharge. None of these symptoms is specific for VVC.

claims.text: Lifetime: 75 percent at least one episode, 40 to 45 percent two or more
claims.quote: An estimated 75% of women will have at least one episode of VVC, and 40%–45% will have two or more episodes.

claims.text: Prior clinician diagnosis does not make self-diagnosis more reliable
claims.quote: Even women who have previously received a diagnosis of VVC by a clinician are not necessarily more likely to be able to diagnose themselves

claims.text: Wet mount with KOH for all symptomatic women; normal pH below 4.5
claims.quote: Candida vaginitis is associated with normal vaginal pH (<4.5). ... Examination of a wet mount with KOH preparation should be performed for all women with symptoms or signs of VVC

claims.text: Candida without symptoms not a reason to treat; 10 to 20 percent carry yeast
claims.quote: Identifying Candida by culture in the absence of symptoms or signs is not an indication for treatment because approximately 10%–20% of women harbor Candida species

claims.text: Uncomplicated VVC not usually sexually acquired; no partner treatment; balanitis treated topically
claims.quote: Uncomplicated VVC is not usually acquired through sexual intercourse, and data do not support treatment of sex partners. A minority of male sex partners have balanitis ... These men benefit from treatment with topical antifungal agents

claims.text: Complicated VVC: no data, no recommendation for partners
claims.quote: No data exist to support treating sex partners of patients with complicated VVC. Therefore, no recommendation can be made.

claims.text: C. albicans azole resistance becoming more common in vaginal isolates
claims.quote: C. albicans azole resistance is becoming more common in vaginal isolates

claims.text: Boric acid regimen eradication about 70 percent
claims.quote: This regimen has clinical and mycologic eradication rates of approximately 70%

claims.text: Topicals: local burning or irritation might occur, usually no systemic side effects; oral azole interactions
claims.quote: Topical agents usually cause no systemic side effects, although local burning or irritation might occur. ... Clinically important interactions can occur when oral azoles are administered with other drugs

claims.text: Oil-based creams and suppositories might weaken latex condoms and diaphragms
claims.quote: The creams and suppositories in these regimens are oil based and might weaken latex condoms and diaphragms.
